title: West Virginia: history overview
d: West Virginia: the Mountain State, admitted 1863 (35th); capital Charleston.
definition: West Virginia: the Mountain State, admitted 1863 (35th); capital Charleston.
description: West Virginia — "Mountain State" — entered the Union 1863 (35th). Its capital is Charleston and its largest city is Charleston. Split from Virginia 1863 (Civil War). This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: West Virginia achieved statehood 1863 (35th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Coal kingdom. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives West Virginia its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How West Virginia went from territory to state.
definition: How West Virginia went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of West Virginia: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. New River Gorge park. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — West Virginia's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Charleston
d: Charleston is the capital of West Virginia.
definition: Charleston is the capital of West Virginia.
description: Charleston has been the seat of West Virginia government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — West Virginia's largest is Charleston — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Mountain State
d: West Virginia is known as "Mountain State."
definition: West Virginia is known as "Mountain State."
description: The nickname "Mountain State" captures how West Virginia sees itself — and how America sees it. Coal built the Mountain State. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Montani semper liberi (Mountaineers are always free)."

title: Motto: Montani semper liberi (Mountaineers are always free)
t: Motto: Montani semper liberi (Mountaineers are always free)
d: The state motto of West Virginia is "Montani semper liberi (Mountaineers are always free)."
definition: The state motto of West Virginia is "Montani semper liberi (Mountaineers are always free)."
description: The motto "Montani semper liberi (Mountaineers are always free)" is West Virginia's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Seal with miner and farmer on blue. Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
